questions.question: Which SQL statement is used to insert multiple rows into a table in a single command?
options: INSERT INTO table VALUES (row1), (row2), (row3)
BATCH INSERT table
ADD ROWS TO table
INSERT MULTIPLE INTO table
questions.answer: INSERT INTO table VALUES (row1), (row2), (row3)

questions.question: What happens if you run DELETE without a WHERE clause?
options: Only the first row is deleted
The table structure is deleted but data remains
All rows in the table are deleted
Nothing happens
questions.answer: All rows in the table are deleted

questions.question: Which statement correctly inserts data into specific columns?
options: INSERT Customers VALUES (CustomerName='Cardinal', City='Stavanger')
INSERT INTO Customers (CustomerName, City) VALUES ('Cardinal', 'Stavanger')
ADD RECORD TO Customers SET CustomerName='Cardinal', City='Stavanger'
INSERT Cardinal, Stavanger INTO Customers (CustomerName, City)
questions.answer: INSERT INTO Customers (CustomerName, City) VALUES ('Cardinal', 'Stavanger')

questions.question: What is the difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE?
options: DELETE is faster than TRUNCATE
DELETE removes rows one by one, TRUNCATE removes all rows at once
DELETE removes table structure, TRUNCATE only removes data
TRUNCATE can be rolled back, DELETE cannot
questions.answer: DELETE removes rows one by one, TRUNCATE removes all rows at once

questions.question: How do you update multiple columns in a single UPDATE statement?
options: UPDATE table SET column1=value1 AND column2=value2 WHERE condition
MODIFY table SET (column1=value1, column2=value2) WHERE condition
UPDATE table SET column1=value1, column2=value2 WHERE condition
UPDATE table column1=value1, column2=value2 WHERE condition
questions.answer: UPDATE table SET column1=value1, column2=value2 WHERE condition

questions.question: Which clause is mandatory in an UPDATE statement?
options: VALUES
FROM
WHERE
SET (to specify what to update)
questions.answer: SET (to specify what to update)

questions.question: What does the RETURNING clause do in an INSERT statement?
options: Checks if the insert was successful
Inserts the same data into another table
Rolls back the transaction if an error occurs
Returns the inserted row(s)
questions.answer: Returns the inserted row(s)

questions.question: How do you delete duplicate rows from a table?
options: DELETE DUPLICATE ROWS FROM table
REMOVE DUPLICATES FROM table
DELETE FROM table WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM table GROUP BY duplicate_column)
DELETE FROM table GROUP BY all_columns HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
questions.answer: DELETE FROM table WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM table GROUP BY duplicate_column)

questions.question: Which INSERT variation allows inserting data from another table?
options: INSERT FROM table2 INTO table1
INSERT INTO table1 SELECT * FROM table2
INSERT INTO table1 VALUES (SELECT * FROM table2)
COPY table2 TO table1
questions.answer: INSERT INTO table1 SELECT * FROM table2

questions.question: What does ON DELETE CASCADE do?
options: Logs the deletion in a separate table
Prevents deletion if related rows exist
Creates a backup before deletion
Automatically deletes related rows in child tables when a parent row is deleted
questions.answer: Automatically deletes related rows in child tables when a parent row is deleted

questions.question: How do you update data based on values from another table?
options: UPDATE FROM table1, table2 SET column = table2.column
UPDATE table1, table2 SET table1.column = table2.column
UPDATE table1 SET column = (SELECT column FROM table2 WHERE condition)
UPDATE table1 JOIN table2 ON condition SET table1.column = table2.column
questions.answer: UPDATE table1 JOIN table2 ON condition SET table1.column = table2.column

questions.question: Which statement inserts NULL values into a column?
options: INSERT INTO table (column1) VALUES (BLANK)
INSERT INTO table (column1) VALUES (NONE)
INSERT INTO table (column1) VALUES (EMPTY)
INSERT INTO table (column1) VALUES (NULL)
questions.answer: INSERT INTO table (column1) VALUES (NULL)

questions.question: How do you prevent SQL injection in INSERT statements?
options: Always use stored procedures
Use parameterized queries/prepared statements
Delete special characters from input
Use double quotes instead of single quotes
questions.answer: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements

questions.question: What is an UPSERT operation?
options: UPDATE then INSERT
INSERT with UPPER case
INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (or MERGE)
DELETE then INSERT
questions.answer: INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (or MERGE)

questions.question: Which clause in UPDATE prevents updating all rows accidentally?
options: LIMIT
WHERE (specifying specific rows)
TOP
FILTER
questions.answer: WHERE (specifying specific rows)

questions.question: How do you insert the current timestamp into a column?
options: INSERT INTO table (timestamp_column) VALUES (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
All of the above (depending on database system)
INSERT INTO table (timestamp_column) VALUES (NOW())
INSERT INTO table (timestamp_column) VALUES (GETDATE())
questions.answer: All of the above (depending on database system)

questions.question: What happens if INSERT violates a UNIQUE constraint?
options: The duplicate row is automatically updated
Only the first occurrence is inserted
The constraint is temporarily disabled
The insert fails with an error
questions.answer: The insert fails with an error

questions.question: How do you delete rows from multiple tables in a single statement?
options: DELETE MULTIPLE table1, table2
DELETE t1, t2 FROM table1 t1 JOIN table2 t2 ON condition
DELETE FROM table1, table2 WHERE condition
DELETE ALL FROM table1 AND table2
questions.answer: DELETE t1, t2 FROM table1 t1 JOIN table2 t2 ON condition

questions.question: Which INSERT statement is most efficient for bulk data?
options: Multiple INSERT VALUES statements
Individual INSERT statements in a loop
INSERT with UNION ALL
BULK INSERT or LOAD DATA INFILE (database-specific)
questions.answer: BULK INSERT or LOAD DATA INFILE (database-specific)

questions.question: How do you update a column by incrementing its current value?
options: UPDATE table SET counter++ WHERE id = 1
UPDATE table SET counter = 1+ WHERE id = 1
UPDATE table INCREMENT counter BY 1 WHERE id = 1
UPDATE table SET counter = counter + 1 WHERE id = 1
questions.answer: UPDATE table SET counter = counter + 1 WHERE id = 1

questions.question: What does the OUTPUT clause do in SQL Server for DML operations?
options: Logs the operation to a file
Returns information about each row affected by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
Creates a backup of affected rows
Optimizes the query execution
questions.answer: Returns information about each row affected by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE

questions.question: How do you insert default values into a table?
options: INSERT DEFAULT INTO table
Both A and B (depending on database system)
INSERT INTO table DEFAULT VALUES
INSERT INTO table VALUES (DEFAULT)
questions.answer: Both A and B (depending on database system)

questions.question: Which DELETE statement deletes rows based on a subquery?
options: DELETE USING table, other_table WHERE condition
DELETE FROM table SUBQUERY (SELECT FROM other_table)
DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM other_table)
DELETE FROM table JOIN other_table ON condition
questions.answer: DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM other_table)

questions.question: How do you update a JSON field in a column?
options: UPDATE table SET json_column.key = 'value'
UPDATE table MODIFY json_column SET key = 'value'
UPDATE table SET json_column->'key' = 'value'
UPDATE table SET json_column = JSON_SET(json_column, '$.key', 'value')
questions.answer: UPDATE table SET json_column = JSON_SET(json_column, '$.key', 'value')

questions.question: What is a MERGE statement?
options: Merges two tables into one
Updates all rows to the same value
Combines two SELECT statements
Combines INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations based on conditions
questions.answer: Combines INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations based on conditions

questions.question: How do you insert a row and get the auto-generated ID back?
options: INSERT ... GET ID
INSERT ... THEN SELECT ID
INSERT ... RETURNING id (or SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() or LAST_INSERT_ID())
INSERT ... OUTPUT INSERTED.id
questions.answer: INSERT ... RETURNING id (or SELECT SCOPE_IDENTITY() or LAST_INSERT_ID())

questions.question: Which UPDATE statement uses a CASE expression?
options: UPDATE table IF condition SET column = value1 ELSE value2
UPDATE table CASE column WHEN condition THEN value1 ELSE value2
UPDATE table SET column = IF(condition, value1, value2)
UPDATE table SET column = CASE WHEN condition THEN value1 ELSE value2 END
questions.answer: UPDATE table SET column = CASE WHEN condition THEN value1 ELSE value2 END

questions.question: How do you delete all rows older than 30 days?
options: DELETE FROM table WHERE date_column OLDER THAN 30 DAYS
DELETE FROM table WHERE date_column < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
DELETE FROM table FILTER date_column PAST 30 DAYS
DELETE FROM table WHERE date_column > NOW() - 30
questions.answer: DELETE FROM table WHERE date_column < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)

questions.question: Which INSERT statement handles errors gracefully?
options: INSERT ... SKIP ON ERROR
INSERT ... ERROR CONTINUE
INSERT ... TRY CATCH
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (PostgreSQL) or INSERT ... IGNORE (MySQL)
questions.answer: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (PostgreSQL) or INSERT ... IGNORE (MySQL)

questions.question: How do you update a BIT/BOOLEAN column?
options: UPDATE table SET active = 1 WHERE id = 1
UPDATE table SET active = 'true' WHERE id = 1
All of the above (depending on database system)
UPDATE table SET active = TRUE WHERE id = 1
questions.answer: All of the above (depending on database system)

questions.question: What does ROLLBACK do after a DELETE?
options: Confirms the deletion
Undoes the delete operation if within a transaction
Deletes additional rows
Creates a backup of deleted rows
questions.answer: Undoes the delete operation if within a transaction

questions.question: How do you insert hierarchical data (parent-child relationships)?
options: INSERT HIERARCHY parent, child
INSERT NESTED parent (child VALUES)
INSERT parent AND child SIMULTANEOUSLY
INSERT parent; then INSERT child with parent's ID
questions.answer: INSERT parent; then INSERT child with parent's ID

questions.question: Which DELETE statement is fastest for large tables?
options: DELETE ALL table
TRUNCATE TABLE (if you want to delete all rows)
DROP AND RECREATE table
DELETE FROM table
questions.answer: TRUNCATE TABLE (if you want to delete all rows)

questions.question: How do you update a column with a random value?
options: Both A and C (depending on need)
UPDATE table SET column = RANDOM()
UPDATE table SET column = NEWID() (for UUID)
UPDATE table SET column = RAND()
questions.answer: Both A and C (depending on need)

questions.question: What does INSERT IGNORE do in MySQL?
options: Logs errors but continues
Skips rows that would cause duplicate key errors
Inserts NULL for all errors
Rolls back the entire insert on any error
questions.answer: Skips rows that would cause duplicate key errors

questions.question: How do you delete rows with a JOIN?
options: DELETE JOIN table1, table2 ON condition
DELETE table1.* FROM table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON condition
DELETE t1 FROM table1 t1 JOIN table2 t2 ON t1.id = t2.id
DELETE FROM table1 USING table2 WHERE table1.id = table2.id
questions.answer: DELETE t1 FROM table1 t1 JOIN table2 t2 ON t1.id = t2.id

questions.question: Which UPDATE statement uses a correlated subquery?
options: UPDATE FROM table1 INNER JOIN table2 ON table1.id = table2.id SET table1.col = table2.col
UPDATE table1 SET col = (SELECT col FROM table2 WHERE table2.id = table1.id)
All of the above can work
UPDATE table1, table2 SET table1.col = table2.col WHERE table1.id = table2.id
questions.answer: UPDATE table1 SET col = (SELECT col FROM table2 WHERE table2.id = table1.id)

questions.question: How do you insert data only if it doesn't exist?
options: INSERT UNIQUE ...
INSERT IF NOT EXISTS ...
INSERT AVOID DUPLICATE ...
INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM table WHERE condition)
questions.answer: INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM table WHERE condition)

questions.question: What is a CTE (Common Table Expression) used with DELETE?
options: DELETE USING CTE table
DELETE CTE FROM table
WITH cte AS (SELECT id FROM table WHERE condition) DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM cte)
DELETE FROM CTE table
questions.answer: WITH cte AS (SELECT id FROM table WHERE condition) DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM cte)

questions.question: How do you update all rows to have sequential numbers?
options: UPDATE table SET id = SEQUENCE()
UPDATE table ORDER BY id SET id = ROW_NUMBER()
UPDATE table SEQUENTIAL id
UPDATE table SET id = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) (may require CTE/temp table)
questions.answer: UPDATE table SET id = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) (may require CTE/temp table)

questions.question: Which INSERT statement uses a UNION ALL?
options: INSERT UNION ALL INTO table VALUES ...
INSERT INTO table SELECT ... UNION ALL SELECT ...
INSERT INTO table UNION ALL VALUES ...
INSERT ALL INTO table UNION SELECT ...
questions.answer: INSERT INTO table SELECT ... UNION ALL SELECT ...

questions.question: How do you delete rows in batches to avoid locking?
options: DELETE BATCH 1000 FROM table
DELETE TOP(1000) FROM table WHERE condition (SQL Server) or LIMIT in other DBs
DELETE FROM table WHERE condition CHUNK 1000
DELETE FROM table WHERE condition IN BATCHES OF 1000
questions.answer: DELETE TOP(1000) FROM table WHERE condition (SQL Server) or LIMIT in other DBs

questions.question: What does ON UPDATE SET NULL do?
options: Prevents updates to parent rows
Sets foreign key columns to NULL when referenced parent row is updated
Deletes child rows when parent is updated
Updates child rows with parent's new value
questions.answer: Sets foreign key columns to NULL when referenced parent row is updated

questions.question: How do you insert a row with an encrypted password?
options: INSERT INTO users (username, password) VALUES ('user', 'pass' ENCRYPTED)
INSERT ENCRYPTED INTO users VALUES ('user', 'pass')
INSERT INTO users (username, password) VALUES ('user', ENCRYPT('pass'))
INSERT INTO users (username, password) ENCRYPT VALUES ('user', 'pass')
questions.answer: INSERT INTO users (username, password) VALUES ('user', ENCRYPT('pass'))

questions.question: Which DELETE statement uses a window function?
options: DELETE WINDOW FUNCTION FROM table
DELETE DUPLICATES USING ROW_NUMBER()
DELETE FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY col ORDER BY id) rn FROM table) WHERE rn > 1
DELETE FROM table WHERE ROW_NUMBER() > 1
questions.answer: DELETE FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY col ORDER BY id) rn FROM table) WHERE rn > 1

questions.question: How do you update a column with its own value modified?
options: UPDATE table SET text_column += ' suffix'
UPDATE table SET text_column = CONCAT(text_column, ' suffix')
UPDATE table SET text_column = text_column || ' suffix'
All of the above (depending on database)
questions.answer: All of the above (depending on database)

questions.question: What does INSERT ... SELECT do?
options: Selects data after inserting
Checks if insert was successful
Inserts rows selected from another table or query
Inserts the result of a SELECT into a variable
questions.answer: Inserts rows selected from another table or query

questions.question: How do you delete rows with a specific pattern in a column?
options: DELETE FROM table WHERE column HAS 'pattern'
DELETE FROM table WHERE column LIKE '%pattern%'
DELETE FROM table PATTERN column = 'pattern'
DELETE FROM table WHERE column CONTAINS 'pattern'
questions.answer: DELETE FROM table WHERE column LIKE '%pattern%'

questions.question: Which UPDATE statement updates from a VALUES list?
options: UPDATE table SET col = VALUES(col) FROM list
UPDATE table USING VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B')
UPDATE table FROM VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B')
UPDATE table SET col = v.col FROM (VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B')) AS v(id, col) WHERE table.id = v.id
questions.answer: UPDATE table SET col = v.col FROM (VALUES (1, 'A'), (2, 'B')) AS v(id, col) WHERE table.id = v.id

questions.question: How do you insert with error logging for failed rows?
options: INSERT INTO table SELECT ... CATCH ERRORS
INSERT INTO table SELECT ... LOG ERRORS INTO err_table
INSERT INTO table SELECT ... WITH ERROR LOGGING
INSERT INTO table SELECT ... OUTPUT ERRORS
questions.answer: INSERT INTO table SELECT ... LOG ERRORS INTO err_table
